sources.text: The 78-layer text decoder uses a BF16 analytical sparse MLA path with absorbed K and V projections. Each layer stores 512 latent and 64 rotary values per token. Only 21 indexer owners append a 128-wide index key; their selected row IDs are carried to the reuse layers in the same forward pass.

Selected rows use the release interleaved RoPE and a BF16 dot-product reference with FP32 scoring. Explicit materialized score tiles model causal useful pairs and rectangular executed work. Active expert weights are read once per distinct selected expert using an upper bound. Router and softmax nonlinear operations and TopK use arithmetic proxies.

Theoretical baseline with untied BF16 token embeddings and full-position output projection. MTP, fused kernels, actual FP8 index packing, RoPE table generation and data-dependent routes are outside this model profile.
Local equations bind the batch, MLA heads, owner routes, expert count and intermediate width from tensor layouts. AllReduce uses the configured ring model.

Shard MLA query heads and their absorbed projections. Replicate the latent and rotary caches and each of the 21 DSA indexers. Reuse selected row IDs within each replica. Reduce the BF16 attention output before its residual add.

Assign equal contiguous expert ranges to EP ranks. Preserve each token’s global Top-K and balance valid routes by quotient and remainder. Each rank reserves ceil(K/EP) slots. Token gathering and weight reads use valid slots. Reduce the BF16 routed output before adding the replicated shared expert.

Shard the intermediate width of each routed expert. Pair gate and up features on each rank and keep every selected expert available. Reduce the BF16 routed output before adding the replicated shared expert.
